simple.meaning: קִלְּשׁוֹן (qillᵉshôwn) is a Hebrew word meaning “a prong , i.e. hay-fork.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קִלְּשׁוֹן (H7053) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קִלְּשׁוֹן (qillᵉshôwn) / H7053 is traced through 1 Samuel 13:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H7053. qilleshon קִלְּשׁוֺן doubtful word, in phrase ק ׳וְלִשְׁלשׁ 1Sam 13:21 (possibly would be fine point , compare Aramaic קלשׁ be thin , hence ׳שׁ ׳ק tridens , E.V. forks , but against analogue, see especially Dr). קָמָה see קום .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to prick ;

occurrences.englishText: The price was one payim† A payim (or pim) was 2/3 shekel of silver, or 0.26 ounces, or 7.6 grams each to sharpen mattocks, plowshares, pitchforks, axes, and goads.
